An indigenous guide to the 2015 federal election

I know two of the candidates, Leona Aglukkaq and Hunter Tootoo. Neither, IMO, would provide proper representation for the riding of Nunavut.

Leona has earned a reputation of doing what her political masters tell her to do, and saying what they tell her to say, when she's told to do or say it. She's also willing to be shown off as an "Aboriginal Minister" instead of a Minister who is Aboriginal and as a result of that she's done very well for herself - there are not a great many people left in Nunavut who respect her, and many of us would be surprised to see her re-elected in October.

Hunter Tootoo ran federally for the NDP in 1997 and placed 3rd but had better luck at the [Nunavut] territorial level, at this point there is not much that can be said to distinguish him from any other territorial MLA. Some might even say that his greatest accomplishment is being a cousin to Jordon Tootoo who plays for the New Jersey Devils.

Speculation within the territory is that he was chosen by the Liberal as their candidate in the upcoming election because he is Aboriginal, looks decent in a suit, and can claim government experience. Unfortunately for Tootoo there are those who remember him throwing his support behind Aglukkaq in the 2011 election campaign and his statements then have come back to somewhat haunt him now. Equally unfortunate for Tootoo is that he is seen by many as a lack luster career politician and political opportunist. He will probably enjoy decent support in the Kivalliq Region where his family originates however there seems to be an underlying feeling in the Baffin Region that he would be little more than another Leona Aglukkaq should he be elected.

Time will tell whether or not territorial distaste for Aglukkaq out weighs a generally ho-hum LPC candidate, time will also tell who the NDP selects as a candidate. Jerry Natanine, current Mayor of Clyde River and vocal opponent to seismic testing in Arctic waters, is looking for the nod - if the NDP wants a candidate with positive name recognition within the Aboriginal community they could do a lot worse.
